definition_en: to form letters or words on a surface, or to compose a text
core_image: 笔尖在纸面上留下一行行痕迹
scene: 考试开始前，女孩先在纸页顶端写下自己的名字。Before the exam began, the girl wrote her own name at the top of the page.
sceneCN: 这里 write 是「写」（第 1 个义项：在纸面上书写文字）；句意：考试开始前，女孩先在纸页顶端写下自己的名字。

senses.title: To form letters on a surface
senses.definition: to form letters or words on paper or another surface
senses.definitionCN: 在纸或其他表面上写出字母或词语
senses.example: Write your name here.
senses.why: The hand moves a point across a surface and leaves a mark, so the verb names the act of tracing words.
senses.whyCN: 手带着一个尖点在表面上移动，留下痕迹，所以这个动词命名的是描出文字的动作。

senses.title: To compose a text
senses.definition: to compose a letter, story or other text
senses.definitionCN: 创作信件、故事或其他文本
senses.example: She wrote a long letter.
senses.why: Once marks become whole sentences, the same verb covers the larger work of composing.
senses.whyCN: 当痕迹连成完整的句子，同一个动词就覆盖了更大的创作工作。

senses.title: To say in writing
senses.definition: to state something in a letter or other written message
senses.definitionCN: 在信件或其他书面消息中说明某事
senses.example: He wrote that he would arrive on Monday.
senses.why: A written message carries the writer's voice, so write can introduce what the text says.
senses.whyCN: 书面消息承载作者的声音，于是 write 可以引出文本所说的内容。

senses.title: To record in writing
senses.definition: to put information into a record or on a board
senses.definitionCN: 把信息写进记录或写在板上
senses.example: The teacher wrote the score on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把分数写在黑板上。
senses.why: Writing fixes a fact so that it can be kept, which gives the sense of recording.
senses.whyCN: 书写把事实固定下来以便保存，由此生出记录的意思。

intro.en: Write first meant to scratch or carve, and only later came to mean marking words with a pen.
intro.cn: write 最初意为刻划、雕刻，后来才指用笔写下文字。

items.en: Writan means to scratch or carve signs into a surface.
items.cn: writan 意为在表面上刻划符号。

items.en: The verb shifts from carving to writing with ink.
items.cn: 这个动词从雕刻转向用墨水书写。

items.en: Write covers letters, books and official records.
items.cn: 近代早期，write 覆盖信件、书籍与正式记录。

items.en: The past forms wrote and written settle into the modern pattern.
items.cn: 现代英语中，过去式 wrote 与过去分词 written 固定下来。

items.en: Write also means to send a written message to someone.
items.cn: 现代英语中，write 也意为给某人写书面消息。

note.en: Write is the act of marking words, while a writer is the person and writing is the result.
note.cn: write 是写下文字的动作，writer 是写的人，writing 是写出的成果。

entries.definition: the activity or result of writing
to set down information for keeping
to create a piece of writing or music

normalIntro.en: Write leaves a trail of marks, and the trail can grow into a letter, a story or a record.
normalIntro.cn: write 留下一串痕迹，这串痕迹可以长成一封信、一个故事或一份记录。

normal.en: Old English writan meant to carve, not yet to write with ink.
normal.cn: 古英语 writan 意为雕刻，还不是用墨水书写。

normal.en: The past tense is wrote, the participle written.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wrote，过去分词是 written。

normal.en: A writer is the person, writing is the result.
normal.cn: writer 是写的人，writing 是写出的成果。

normal.en: Write down fixes a thought on paper.
normal.cn: write down 把一个想法固定在纸上。

normal.en: Write to a friend means send a letter.
normal.cn: write to a friend 意为给朋友写信。

abstract.en: Picture a pen tip drawing one line after another.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖一笔接一笔地画出线条。

abstract.en: See a blank page slowly filling with words.
abstract.cn: 想象空白纸页慢慢被文字填满。

abstract.en: Think of a chisel cutting a mark into stone.
abstract.cn: 想象凿子把痕迹刻进石头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莱特」——莱特兄弟把飞行计划写满纸页；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 writan，原意为刻划、雕刻，后转为书写。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with marks on a surface and grows into composing, messaging and keeping records.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从表面上的痕迹开始，长成创作、传递消息与保存记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen tip leaving a trail of marks on paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔尖在纸上留下一串痕迹。

branches.en: The base sense forms letters on a surface.
branches.cn: 基本义在表面上写出字母。

branches.en: Marks joined into sentences become composing.
branches.cn: 痕迹连成句子就变成创作。

branches.en: A written text can carry a message to a reader.
branches.cn: 书面文本能把消息带给读者。

branches.en: Writing fixes information so that it can be kept.
branches.cn: 书写把信息固定下来以便保存。

branches.en: All three start from a mark made on purpose.
branches.cn: 三者都从有意留下的痕迹开始。

intro.en: Write is a native verb with irregular forms and English derivations such as writer and rewrite.
intro.cn: write 是本土动词，形式不规则，也能派生出 writer、rewrite 等。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in write; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: write 没有拉丁成分，这个词属日耳曼语。

items.example: Writan is the Old English ancestor of write.
items.exampleCN: writan 是 write 的古英语祖先。

definition_en: to move quickly on foot, to operate, to manage, or to flow
core_image: 双腿快速交替，身体向前冲出去
scene: 下课铃一响，孩子们就冲过操场。The bell rang, and the children ran across the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 run 是「跑」（第 1 个义项：用双脚快速前进）；句意：下课铃一响，孩子们就冲过操场。

senses.title: To move quickly on foot
senses.definition: to move quickly on foot, faster than walking
senses.definitionCN: 用双脚快速移动，比走快
senses.example: I run every morning.
senses.why: The legs alternate quickly and the body tips forward, so the verb names speed driven by the feet.
senses.whyCN: 双腿快速交替，身体向前倾，所以这个动词命名的是由双脚驱动的速度。

senses.title: To operate
senses.definition: to work or operate, especially of a machine or program
senses.definitionCN: 工作、运转，尤指机器或程序
senses.example: The machine runs well.
senses.why: A machine keeps moving through its cycle the way legs keep moving, so the verb extends to operation.
senses.whyCN: 机器按循环持续运转，就像双腿持续交替，于是这个词延伸到运行。

senses.title: To manage
senses.definition: to manage or operate a business or organization
senses.definitionCN: 经营或管理一项生意或组织
senses.example: She runs a small shop.
senses.why: Keeping a business going is like keeping a machine running, so management borrows the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 让生意持续下去就像让机器持续运转，于是管理借用了同一个动词。

senses.title: To flow
senses.definition: to flow or extend in a certain direction, as a river does
senses.definitionCN: 像河流一样朝某方向流动或延伸
senses.example: The river runs through the town.
senses.why: Water moving steadily along a channel looks like a runner following a course, so flow takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 水沿着河道持续前进，像一个跑者沿着路线奔跑，于是流动也用同一个词。

intro.en: Run is an old Germanic verb of quick movement that widened to machines, business and water.
intro.cn: run 是古老的日耳曼语快速移动动词，词义扩展到机器、生意与水流。

items.en: Rinnan and iernan both mean to run or flow.
items.cn: rinnan 与 iernan 都意为跑或流动。

items.en: The forms merge and the past tense becomes ran.
items.cn: 两个形式合并，过去式成为 ran。

items.en: Run extends to the working of machines.
items.cn: 近代早期，run 扩展到机器的运转。

items.en: Run a business means manage it.
items.cn: 现代英语中，run a business 意为经营生意。

items.en: Rivers and liquids still run in the oldest sense.
items.cn: 河流与液体仍使用最古老的意义「流动」。

note.en: Run is fast movement, jog is a gentle run, and operate is the machine sense.
note.cn: run 是快速移动，jog 是慢跑，operate 对应机器运转义。

normalIntro.en: Run starts with legs in motion and stretches to machines, shops and rivers.
normalIntro.cn: run 从双腿运动开始，延伸到机器、店铺与河流。

normal.en: The past tense is ran, the participle run.
normal.cn: 过去式是 ran，过去分词是 run。

normal.en: Run away means escape on foot.
normal.cn: run away 意为跑开、逃跑。

normal.en: Run out of means use up.
normal.cn: run out of 意为用完。

normal.en: A machine runs, a shop is run.
normal.cn: 机器 run 是运转，店铺 is run 是被经营。

normal.en: A river runs through a town.
normal.cn: 河流 run through 镇子，即穿流而过。

abstract.en: Picture legs blurring as the body leans forward.
abstract.cn: 想象双腿快成一片模糊，身体前倾。

abstract.en: See a wheel turning steadily in a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象机器里一个轮子稳定转动。

abstract.en: Think of water sliding along a narrow channel.
abstract.cn: 想象水沿着窄河道滑行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嚷」——跑得太快，风在耳边直嚷；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 rinnan 与 iernan 合并而来，与德语 rennen 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers feet, machines, businesses and rivers because each keeps moving along a course.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词覆盖双脚、机器、生意与河流，因为它们都沿着某条路线持续运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: legs alternating fast while the body drives forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：双腿快速交替，身体向前冲。

branches.en: The base sense is quick movement on foot.
branches.cn: 基本义是用双脚快速移动。

branches.en: A machine repeating its cycle is said to run.
branches.cn: 机器重复循环被说成 run。

branches.en: Keeping a business going borrows the machine image.
branches.cn: 让生意持续经营借用了机器的画面。

branches.en: Water following a channel also follows a course.
branches.cn: 水沿河道前进，也像沿着路线奔跑。

branches.en: All three share continuous motion along a path.
branches.cn: 三者共享沿路径的持续运动。

intro.en: Run is a native verb that forms runner and phrasal verbs with away, out and into.
intro.cn: run 是本土动词，可构成 runner，并与 away、out、into 组成短语动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in run; its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: run 没有拉丁成分，其亲属词属日耳曼语。

items.example: Rinnan is one Old English ancestor of run.
items.exampleCN: rinnan 是 run 的一个古英语祖先。

items.example: Run out of means use up.
items.exampleCN: run out of 意为用完。

items.example: Run into means meet by chance.
items.exampleCN: run into 意为偶然遇到。

definition_en: a piece of soft material used to rub out pencil marks, or the material itself
core_image: 一块软软的胶，把铅笔痕迹一点点蹭掉
scene: 写错答案后，男孩拿起橡皮轻轻擦掉。After writing the wrong answer, the boy picked up a rubber and rubbed it out gently.
sceneCN: 这里 rubber 是「橡皮」（第 1 个义项：擦除铅笔痕迹的软胶块）；句意：写错答案后，男孩拿起橡皮轻轻擦掉。

senses.title: A piece for rubbing out marks
senses.definition: a small piece of soft material used to rub out pencil marks
senses.definitionCN: 用来擦掉铅笔痕迹的小块软材料
senses.example: May I borrow your rubber?
senses.why: The thing is named by what it does: it rubs marks away, so the verb rub plus the agent ending gives the object.
senses.whyCN: 这件东西按它的作用命名：它把痕迹蹭掉，于是动词 rub 加表示施动者的词尾就成了这个名词。

senses.title: The elastic material
senses.definition: the elastic material made from the juice of a tropical tree
senses.definitionCN: 由热带树木汁液制成的弹性材料
senses.example: The ball is made of rubber.
senses.why: The same material that rubs out marks is also elastic, so rubber names the substance as well as the eraser.
senses.whyCN: 能擦掉痕迹的同一种材料也有弹性，于是 rubber 既指橡皮，也指这种物质。

senses.title: A tyre in informal speech
senses.definition: a tyre, usually in the plural in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 轮胎，英式口语中常用复数
senses.example: The car needs new rubbers.
senses.why: Tyres are made of the same material, so in casual speech the material's name stands for the object.
senses.whyCN: 轮胎由同一种材料制成，于是口语中用材料名代指这个物件。

intro.en: Rubber was first a name for anything that rubs, then for the eraser, and later for the elastic material.
intro.cn: rubber 起初指任何用来蹭擦的东西，后来指橡皮，再后来指弹性材料。

items.en: Rubber names a person or thing that rubs.
items.cn: rubber 指擦拭的人或物。

items.en: The word is applied to a piece of material for rubbing out pencil marks.
items.cn: 这个词被用来指擦除铅笔痕迹的材料块。

items.en: Rubber comes to name the elastic substance from tropical trees.
items.cn: rubber 开始指来自热带树木的弹性物质。

items.en: Rubber covers erasers, the raw material and products such as boots.
items.cn: 现代英语中，rubber 覆盖橡皮、原料以及靴子等制品。

items.en: In informal British speech rubbers can mean tyres.
items.cn: 英式口语中 rubbers 可以指轮胎。

note.en: Rubber is the material or eraser, while eraser is the American word for the same tool.
note.cn: rubber 指材料或橡皮，eraser 是同一工具的美式说法。

entries.definition: to move something back and forth over a surface
the American word for a rubber
the milky juice used to make rubber
the rubber ring around a wheel

normalIntro.en: Rubber is literally the thing that rubs, and the same name stretches to the elastic material.
normalIntro.cn: rubber 字面上就是「用来蹭擦的东西」，同一个名字又延伸到弹性材料。

normal.en: Rub plus -er gives rubber, the thing that rubs.
normal.cn: rub 加 -er 构成 rubber，用来擦的东西。

normal.en: A rubber rubs out pencil marks.
normal.cn: 橡皮把铅笔痕迹擦掉。

normal.en: Rubber also means the elastic material.
normal.cn: rubber 也指有弹性的橡胶。

normal.en: A rubber band stretches and snaps back.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋拉开后会弹回。

normal.en: In British English a rubber is an eraser.
normal.cn: 英式英语中 a rubber 就是橡皮。

abstract.en: Picture a grey block wearing a pencil mark away.
abstract.cn: 想象一块灰胶把铅笔痕一点点磨掉。

abstract.en: See a rubber band pulled long between two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象橡皮筋在两根手指间被拉长。

abstract.en: Think of milky juice dripping from a rubber tree.
abstract.cn: 想象橡胶树滴下乳白的汁液。

examples.en: The ball is made of rubber.

examples.cn: 橡胶靴能让脚保持干燥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉伯」——一块能拉长又弹回的胶；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由动词 rub 加 -er 构成，原意为「擦拭之物」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from the tool that rubs out marks to the material itself and then to products made of it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从擦除痕迹的工具，转到材料本身，再转到用这种材料制成的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft block wearing a pencil mark away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块软胶把铅笔痕一点点蹭掉。

branches.en: The base sense is the small block used to rub out marks.
branches.cn: 基本义是用来擦掉痕迹的小块。

branches.en: The same material is named for its elasticity.
branches.cn: 同一种材料因弹性而得名。

branches.en: Products made of the material borrow its name.
branches.cn: 用这种材料制成的产品借用它的名字。

branches.en: Tool and material share one origin in the verb rub.
branches.cn: 工具与材料都源于动词 rub。

branches.en: The material and the tyre are linked by what they are made of.
branches.cn: 材料与轮胎因制作原料而相连。

intro.en: Rubber is built from the verb rub plus -er, and then takes further endings such as -y and -ize.
intro.cn: rubber 由动词 rub 加 -er 构成，随后又能接 -y、-ize 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in rubber; both the verb and the ending are English.
latinIntro.cn: rubber 没有拉丁成分，动词与词尾都属英语。

items.example: Rub is the verb behind rubber.
items.exampleCN: rub 是 rubber 背后的动词。

items.meaning: one or a thing that does
items.example: The ending -er turns rub into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 把 rub 变成一件东西。

items.example: Rubber names both the tool and the material.
items.exampleCN: rubber 既指工具也指材料。

items.example: Rubber band joins the material with a shape.
items.exampleCN: rubber band 把材料与形状结合。

definition_en: the star that gives light and heat to the earth, or the light from it
core_image: 一轮炽热的圆盘挂在天上，把光撒向地面
scene: 雨停后，云层散开，太阳照在湿漉漉的路面上。After the rain stopped, the clouds opened and the sun shone on the wet road.
sceneCN: 这里 sun 是「太阳」（第 1 个义项：给地球光和热的恒星）；句意：雨停后，云层散开，太阳照在湿漉漉的路面上。

senses.title: The star at the centre of our system
senses.definition: the star that gives light and heat to the earth
senses.definitionCN: 给地球提供光和热的恒星
senses.example: The sun is bright today.
senses.why: One hot disc rises, crosses the sky and sets, so the word names the single body that rules the day.
senses.whyCN: 一个炽热的圆盘升起、越过天空又落下，于是这个词命名那个支配白昼的唯一天体。

senses.title: The light and warmth
senses.definition: the light and warmth that come from the sun
senses.definitionCN: 来自太阳的光和热
senses.example: We sat in the sun.
senses.why: What the body feels is the light itself, so the name of the body also names its warmth.
senses.whyCN: 身体感受到的是光本身，于是天体的名字也指它的温暖。

senses.title: Any star of its kind
senses.definition: any star, especially one with planets around it
senses.definitionCN: 任何恒星，尤指带有行星的恒星
senses.example: Many suns shine in the night sky.
senses.exampleCN: 夜空中许多恒星在闪耀。
senses.why: Once the sun is understood as one star among many, the word can stand for stars in general.
senses.whyCN: 一旦太阳被理解为众多恒星中的一颗，这个词就能泛指恒星。

intro.en: Sun is one of the oldest English words, unchanged in shape for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: sun 是英语最古老的词之一，一千多年来形状几乎未变。

items.en: The ancestor form sunnon names the sun.
items.cn: 祖语形式 sunnon 指太阳。

items.en: Sunne is the common word for the sun.
items.cn: sunne 是古英语中指太阳的常用词。

items.en: The spelling shortens to sun and the word keeps its meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写缩为 sun，词义不变。

items.en: Sun also names sunlight and warmth.
items.cn: 现代英语中，sun 也指阳光与温暖。

items.en: Astronomy uses sun for stars of the same kind.
items.cn: 天文学用 sun 指同类恒星。

note.en: Sun is the body, sunlight is what reaches us, and star is the wider class.
note.cn: sun 是天体，sunlight 是到达我们的光，star 是更大的类别。

entries.definition: a burning ball of gas in space
entries.definitionCN: 太空中燃烧的气体球，恒星

entries.definition: the light that comes from the sun

normalIntro.en: Sun is the body in the sky, and the same word covers the light and warmth it sends.
normalIntro.cn: sun 是天上的天体，同一个词也覆盖它送来的光与热。

normal.en: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
normal.cn: 太阳从东边升起，从西边落下。

normal.en: In the sun means in sunlight.
normal.cn: in the sun 意为在阳光下。

normal.en: Sunny adds -y to sun.
normal.cn: sunny 在 sun 后加 -y。

normal.en: Sunshine joins sun with shine.
normal.cn: sunshine 把 sun 与 shine 结合。

normal.en: Under the sun means anywhere in the world.
normal.cn: under the sun 意为天底下任何地方。

abstract.en: Picture a hot disc rising over a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一轮炽热的圆盘从山后升起。

abstract.en: See warm light falling across a floor.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖的光洒在地板上。

abstract.en: Think of a single lamp that lights the whole sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏照亮整片天空的灯。

examples.en: The sun rises in the east.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伞」——阳光太强时要打伞；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sunne，与德语 Sonne、拉丁语 sol 同出一支远古印欧语词根。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the body, the light it gives, and by extension any star of the same kind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词命名天体、它送来的光，并延伸指任何同类恒星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hot disc in the sky pouring light onto the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：天上一轮炽热的圆盘把光倾泻到地面。

branches.en: The base sense is the single star that lights the earth.
branches.cn: 基本义是照亮地球的那颗恒星。

branches.en: The light and warmth it sends take the same name.
branches.cn: 它送来的光与热使用同一个名字。

branches.en: Astronomy widens the word to stars in general.
branches.cn: 天文学把这个词扩展到泛指恒星。

branches.en: Body and light are one experience on a bright day.
branches.cn: 晴天里，天体与光是一种体验。

branches.cn: 唯一的太阳成为许多恒星的范本。

intro.en: Sun is a native stem that forms sunny, sunshine and sunless.
intro.cn: sun 是本土词干，可构成 sunny、sunshine、sunless。

latinIntro.en: Latin sol is a distant cognate of sun, not a borrowed element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sol 是 sun 的远亲，而非借入成分。

items.example: Sunne is the Old English ancestor of sun.
items.exampleCN: sunne 是 sun 的古英语祖先。
sunshine 把 sun 与 shine 结合。

items.example: Sunbathe means lie in the sun.
Sun hat joins the sun with a covering.
items.exampleCN: sun hat 把太阳与遮头之物结合。

definition_en: the natural body that circles the earth and shines at night, or any such body
core_image: 一枚安静的银盘挂在夜空中
scene: 夜里，海面上方挂着一轮又圆又白的月亮。That night a full white moon hung above the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 moon 是「月亮」（第 1 个义项：环绕地球的天然天体）；句意：夜里，海面上方挂着一轮又圆又白的月亮。

derivatives.zh: 蜜月，由 honey 与 moon 复合

senses.title: The body that circles the earth
senses.definition: the natural body that circles the earth and shines at night
senses.definitionCN: 环绕地球、在夜间发亮的天然天体
senses.example: The moon is bright tonight.
senses.why: A pale disc appears in the night sky and slowly changes shape, so the word names the one companion of the night.
senses.whyCN: 一个苍白的圆盘出现在夜空并慢慢变形，于是这个词命名夜晚唯一的伴侣。

senses.title: A natural satellite
senses.definition: a natural body that circles a planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕行星运行的天然天体
senses.example: The earth has one moon.
senses.why: Once other planets are known to have companions, the word widens from our moon to satellites in general.
senses.whyCN: 一旦知道其他行星也有伴侣，这个词就从我们的月亮扩展到泛指卫星。

senses.title: A month in old use
senses.definition: a month, used in old or poetic speech
senses.definitionCN: 一个月，用于古老或诗意的说法
senses.example: That happened many moons ago.
senses.why: The moon completes a cycle in about a month, so people once counted time by moons.
senses.whyCN: 月亮大约一个月完成一次圆缺，所以人们曾用月亮来数时间。

intro.en: Moon is an old Germanic word, and the moon once served as the clock of the month.
intro.cn: moon 是古老的日耳曼语词，月亮曾经充当月份的钟表。

items.en: The ancestor form menon names the moon.
items.cn: 祖语形式 menon 指月亮。

items.en: Mona is the common word for the moon.
items.cn: mona 是古英语中指月亮的常用词。

items.en: The spelling settles as moon and the old ending weakens.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 moon，古老词尾弱化。

items.en: Moonlight and moonlit grow from the same stem.
items.cn: moonlight 与 moonlit 从同一词干生长出来。

items.en: Astronomy uses moon for any natural satellite.
items.cn: 现代天文学用 moon 指任何天然卫星。

note.en: Moon is the body, moonlight is its light, and satellite is the wider astronomical term.
note.cn: moon 是天体，moonlight 是它的光，satellite 是更广的天文学术语。

entries.definition: twelve o'clock in the middle of the day
a body that circles a planet
the curved shape of a thin moon

normalIntro.en: Moon is the night's pale disc, and the same word stretches to satellites and to months.
normalIntro.cn: moon 是夜里苍白的圆盘，同一个词又延伸到卫星与月份。

normal.en: A full moon is round, a new moon is dark.
normal.cn: 满月是圆的，新月是暗的。

normal.en: Moonlight joins moon with light.
normal.cn: moonlight 把 moon 与 light 结合。

normal.en: The earth has one moon.
normal.cn: 地球有一颗卫星。

normal.en: Many moons ago means a long time ago.
normal.cn: many moons ago 意为很久以前。

normal.en: A honeymoon joins honey and moon.
normal.cn: honeymoon 把 honey 与 moon 结合。

abstract.en: Picture a silver plate floating in black water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只银盘浮在黑水上。

abstract.en: See a thin curve of light in a dark sky.
abstract.cn: 想象暗空中一道细细的亮弧。

abstract.en: Think of a slow clock that changes shape each night.
abstract.cn: 想象一座每晚改变形状的慢钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「慕」——人们仰望夜空，心生爱慕；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 mona，与德语 Mond、拉丁语 mensis（月）同出一支远古词根。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with the earth's companion, widens to any satellite, and echoes an old way of counting months.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从地球的伴侣开始，扩展到任何卫星，并回响着古老的计月方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale silver disc hanging in the night sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚苍白的银盘挂在夜空。

branches.en: The base sense is the body that circles the earth.
branches.cn: 基本义是环绕地球的天体。

branches.en: The word widens to natural satellites of any planet.
branches.cn: 这个词扩展到任何行星的天然卫星。

branches.en: Its cycle once measured the month.
branches.cn: 它的圆缺周期曾用来量度月份。

branches.en: Our moon is the model for every satellite.
branches.cn: 我们的月亮是每颗卫星的范本。

branches.en: The changing disc and the month share one cycle.
branches.cn: 变化的圆盘与月份共享同一个周期。

intro.en: Moon is a native stem that forms moonlight, moonlit and honeymoon.
intro.cn: moon 是本土词干，可构成 moonlight、moonlit、honeymoon。

latinIntro.en: Latin mensis, meaning month, is a distant cognate of moon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mensis（月）是 moon 的远亲。

items.example: Mona is the Old English ancestor of moon.
items.exampleCN: mona 是 moon 的古英语祖先。
moonlight 把 moon 与 light 结合。

items.example: Moonlit means lit by the moon.
items.exampleCN: moonlit 意为被月光照亮的。
honeymoon 把 honey 与 moon 结合。
moony 意为像月光般梦幻的。

items.example: Moon cake joins the moon with a festival food.
items.exampleCN: moon cake 把月亮与节令食品结合。

definition_en: the early part of the day, from sunrise until noon
core_image: 天刚亮，光从窗边慢慢铺进屋里
scene: 窗外的鸟每天早晨都在枝头唱歌。The birds outside the window sing every morning on the branch.
sceneCN: 这里 morning 是「早晨」（第 1 个义项：一天中日出前后的一段时间）；句意：窗外的鸟每天早晨都在枝头唱歌。

senses.title: The early part of the day
senses.definition: the early part of the day, from sunrise until about noon
senses.definitionCN: 一天中从日出到中午前后的一段时间
senses.example: I get up early in the morning.
senses.why: Light returns and the world wakes, so the word names the stretch of day that follows the dark.
senses.whyCN: 光回来了，世界醒来，于是这个词命名黑暗之后的那一段白昼。

senses.title: The whole forenoon
senses.definition: the time before noon, including the later part of the forenoon
senses.definitionCN: 中午之前的时间，包括上午后半段
senses.example: The meeting lasted all morning.
senses.why: Morning stretches from first light to noon, so it can cover the whole block of time before lunch.
senses.whyCN: morning 从第一缕光延伸到正午，因此可以涵盖午饭前的整段时间。

senses.title: A spoken greeting
senses.definition: a short greeting used in the morning
senses.definitionCN: 早晨使用的简短问候
senses.example: Morning, everyone!
senses.why: The name of the time becomes a greeting, as if the speaker were handing over the morning itself.
senses.whyCN: 时间的名字变成问候语，仿佛说话人把整个早晨递了过去。

intro.en: Morning is built on an old Germanic word for the dawn and has named the early day for centuries.
intro.cn: morning 建立在一个古老的日耳曼语「黎明」词上，数百年来一直指清晨。

items.en: The ancestor form murgana refers to the morning.
items.cn: 祖语形式 murgana 指早晨。

items.en: Morgen means morning, and the word is already common.
items.cn: morgen 意为早晨，这个词当时已很常用。

items.en: The ending -ing is added and the form becomes morning.
items.cn: 中古英语中加上词尾 -ing，形成 morning。

items.en: Good morning becomes the standard polite greeting.
items.cn: 近代早期，good morning 成为标准的礼貌问候。

items.en: Morning still means the hours before noon.
items.cn: 现代英语中，morning 仍指正午之前的时段。

note.en: Morning is the early day, dawn is the first light, and mourning is a sad homophone.
note.cn: morning 是清晨时段，dawn 是第一缕光，mourning 是同音的「哀悼」。

entries.definition: the experience of sadness after a death
the first light of the day
the moment when the day begins

normalIntro.en: Morning is the daylight half before noon, and its greeting is simply the name of that time.
normalIntro.cn: morning 是正午之前的那半段白昼，而它的问候语就是这段时间的名字。

normal.en: Good morning is the standard early greeting.
normal.cn: good morning 是标准的早晨问候。

normal.en: In the morning means before noon.
normal.cn: in the morning 意为中午以前。

normal.en: Mornings is used for several mornings.
normal.cn: mornings 用于多个早晨。

normal.en: Mourning sounds the same but means grief.
normal.cn: mourning 读音相同，但意为哀悼。

normal.en: Midmorning is the middle of the morning.
normal.cn: midmorning 是上午的中段。

abstract.en: Picture pale light spreading across a bedroom floor.
abstract.cn: 想象淡光铺满卧室地板。

abstract.en: See birds singing on a branch at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象第一缕光里鸟儿在枝头鸣叫。

abstract.en: Think of a clock still far from noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一座离正午还远的钟。

examples.en: I get up early in the morning.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸宁」——早晨摸一摸还带着凉意的窗台；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 morgen，与德语 Morgen 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers the early day, the whole forenoon, and the greeting that borrows its name.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖清晨、整个上午，以及借用其名字的问候语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pale light spreading into a room at daybreak.
core.cn: 核心意象：破晓时淡光铺进房间。

branches.en: The base sense is the early day after sunrise.
branches.cn: 基本义是日出后的清晨。

branches.en: The same span widens to the whole forenoon.
branches.cn: 同一时段扩展到整个上午。

branches.en: The name of the time becomes a greeting.
branches.cn: 时间的名字变成问候语。

branches.en: Both describe the hours before noon.
branches.cn: 两者都描述正午前的时段。

branches.en: The greeting hands over the morning itself.
branches.cn: 问候语把早晨本身递给对方。

intro.en: Morning is built on the old stem morgen plus the noun ending -ing.
intro.cn: morning 由古老词干 morgen 加名词词尾 -ing 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in morning; the stem is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: morning 没有拉丁成分，词干属日耳曼语。

items.example: Morgen is the Old English ancestor of morning.
items.exampleCN: morgen 是 morning 的古英语祖先。
good morning 以 good 开头。

items.example: Midmorning means the middle of the morning.
Early morning names the first hours.
items.exampleCN: early morning 指最早的几个小时。

items.meaning: a drink, or a light meal
items.example: Morning tea joins the time with a meal.
items.exampleCN: morning tea 把时段与茶点结合。

definition_zh: 紫色；紫色的；辞藻华丽的
definition_en: a colour between red and blue, or having that colour
core_image: 红与蓝慢慢调在一起，变成深沉的紫
scene: 女孩穿着一条紫色连衣裙去参加聚会。The girl wore a purple dress to the party.
sceneCN: 这里 purple 是「紫色的」（第 2 个义项：作形容词，表示颜色）；句意：女孩穿着一条紫色连衣裙去参加聚会。

senses.title: The colour itself
senses.definition: a colour made by mixing red and blue
senses.definitionCN: 红与蓝混合而成的颜色
senses.example: Purple is my favourite colour.
senses.exampleCN: 紫色是我最喜欢的颜色。
senses.why: Two strong colours meet and settle into one deep shade, so the word names the meeting point of red and blue.
senses.whyCN: 两种强烈的颜色相遇，沉淀成一种深色，于是这个词命名红与蓝的交汇处。

senses.title: Having that colour
senses.definition: having the colour purple
senses.definitionCN: 具有紫色的
senses.example: The sky turned purple at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时天空变成了紫色。
senses.why: The name of the colour works directly as an adjective, so no ending is needed to describe a thing.
senses.whyCN: 颜色的名字直接充当形容词，因此描述事物时不需要另加词尾。

senses.title: Overly ornate writing
senses.definition: too elaborate or ornate, especially of writing
senses.definitionCN: 过于华丽雕琢，尤指文句
senses.example: His purple prose impressed nobody.
senses.exampleCN: 他那套华丽辞藻没有打动任何人。
senses.why: Purple dye was once rare and splendid, so the colour's richness came to describe writing that tries too hard to be splendid.
senses.whyCN: 紫色染料曾经稀有而华贵，于是这种颜色的富丽被用来形容过分追求华美的文字。

intro.en: Purple comes from the name of a costly dye made from sea snails in the ancient world.
intro.cn: purple 来自古代用海螺制成的昂贵染料之名。

items.en: Porphyra names the purple dye and the shellfish that produced it.
items.cn: porphyra 指紫色染料及产生它的贝类。

items.en: Purpura is the Latin name for the dye and the colour.
items.cn: purpura 是这种染料与颜色的拉丁名。

items.en: Purpul appears as a borrowed word for the rich colour.
items.cn: purpul 作为借词出现，指这种华贵的颜色。

items.en: The spelling settles as purple.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写定为 purple。

items.en: Purple also describes overly ornate writing.
items.cn: 现代英语中，purple 也形容过分华丽的文句。

note.en: Purple is the broad colour, while violet and mauve name narrower shades.
note.cn: purple 是宽泛的紫色，violet 与 mauve 指更具体的色调。

normalIntro.en: Purple sits between red and blue, and its ancient dye was rare enough to mark rank.
normalIntro.cn: purple 位于红与蓝之间，古代染料稀有到足以标记身份。

normal.en: Mix red and blue to get purple.
normal.cn: 红与蓝混合就得到紫色。

normal.en: Purple is both a noun and an adjective.
normal.cn: purple 既可作名词也可作形容词。

normal.en: Purplish means slightly purple.
normal.cn: purplish 意为略带紫色。

normal.en: Purple prose means writing that is too ornate.
normal.cn: purple prose 指过分华丽的文字。

normal.en: The comparative is purpler, the superlative purplest.
normal.cn: 比较级是 purpler，最高级是 purplest。

abstract.en: Picture red and blue paint swirling into one shade.
abstract.cn: 想象红蓝颜料旋成一种颜色。

abstract.en: See a deep robe worn by a ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一位统治者穿的深色长袍。

abstract.en: Think of a dusk sky fading from pink to violet.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏天空从粉红褪成紫罗兰。

examples.cn: 紫色是我最喜欢的颜色。

examples.en: The sky turned purple at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时天空变成了紫色。

root: 希腊语 porphyra 经拉丁语 purpura 借入英语，原指海螺制成的紫色染料。

sensesIntro.en: The colour works as a noun and an adjective, and its old splendour adds the sense of ornate writing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个颜色既能作名词也能作形容词，其古老的华贵又添上「辞藻华丽」一义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red and blue blending into one deep shade.
core.cn: 核心意象：红与蓝融成一种深色。

branches.en: The base sense is the colour between red and blue.
branches.cn: 基本义是红蓝之间的颜色。

branches.en: The colour name works directly as an adjective.
branches.cn: 颜色名直接充当形容词。

branches.en: The old splendour of the dye becomes a comment on ornate writing.
branches.cn: 染料昔日的华贵变成对华丽文字的评语。

branches.en: Noun and adjective share the same colour.
branches.cn: 名词与形容词共享同一种颜色。

branches.en: The rare dye links the colour to richness of style.
branches.cn: 稀有染料把颜色与文风富丽联系起来。

intro.en: Purple is a borrowed colour word that takes English endings such as -ish and -ness.
intro.cn: purple 是借入的颜色词，可接 -ish、-ness 等英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source purpura is the direct ancestor of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源 purpura 是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: Purpura is the Latin source of purple.
items.exampleCN: purpura 是 purple 的拉丁来源。
purpled 意为被染成紫色的。

items.example: Violet is a close neighbour of purple.
items.exampleCN: violet 是 purple 的近邻色。

definition_en: the day of the week after Sunday and before Tuesday
core_image: 一周的门被推开，第一天的光透进来
scene: 课程表上，第一节音乐课排在星期一。On the timetable, the first music lesson is on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 Monday 是「星期一」（第 1 个义项：一周中的第二天、通常的工作日开端）；句意：课程表上，第一节音乐课排在星期一。

senses.title: The day after Sunday
senses.definition: the day of the week after Sunday and before Tuesday
senses.definitionCN: 星期日之后、星期二之前的那一天
senses.example: Monday is the first day of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 星期一是一周的第一天。
senses.why: The day is named after the moon, and in the English week it opens the working stretch.
senses.whyCN: 这一天以月亮命名，在英语的一周里它开启工作的那一段。

senses.title: The start of the working week
senses.definition: the day seen as the beginning of work or school after the weekend
senses.definitionCN: 周末之后开始工作或上学的第一天
senses.example: Monday marks a fresh start for many people.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多人来说，星期一是新的开始。
senses.why: After the rest of the weekend, the first working day carries the feeling of a beginning.
senses.whyCN: 经过周末的休息，第一个工作日带着「开始」的感觉。

senses.title: Every Monday
senses.definition: used in the plural for something that happens each Monday
senses.definitionCN: 用复数表示每逢星期一发生的事
senses.example: Mondays are always busy at the office.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室每逢周一总是很忙。
senses.why: A repeated day becomes a pattern, so the plural names the habit rather than one date.
senses.whyCN: 重复出现的一天变成一种规律，于是复数命名的是习惯而不是某个日期。

intro.en: Monday is the moon's day, a name borrowed from Latin and reshaped in Old English.
intro.cn: Monday 是「月亮之日」，这个名字借自拉丁语，又在古英语中改写。

items.en: Dies Lunae means the day of the moon.
items.cn: dies Lunae 意为月亮之日。

items.en: The day is called Monandæg, the moon's day.
items.cn: 这一天叫 Monandæg，即月亮之日。

items.en: The spelling settles toward Monday.
items.cn: 中古英语中拼写逐渐定为 Monday。

items.en: Monday is fixed as the first working day in the English week.
items.cn: 近代早期，Monday 固定为英语一周中的第一个工作日。

items.en: Monday blues names the low mood of returning to work.
items.cn: 现代英语中，Monday blues 指重返工作的低落情绪。

note.en: Monday opens the working week, while Tuesday and Sunday sit on either side of it.
note.cn: Monday 开启工作周，Tuesday 与 Sunday 分列两侧。

entries.definition: the written short form of Monday
more than one Monday, or every Monday
entries.definitionCN: 多个星期一；每逢星期一

entries.definition: any day from Monday to Friday
a day on which people work

normalIntro.en: Monday is the moon's day and the gate into the working week.

definition_en: the second month of the year, between January and March
core_image: 冬末的雨落在还没醒来的街道上
scene: 二月常常下雨，我们出门都带伞。February is often rainy, so we take umbrellas when we go out.
sceneCN: 这里 February 是「二月」（第 1 个义项：一年中的第二个月，在一月与三月之间）；句意：二月常常下雨，我们出门都带伞。

senses.title: The second month of the year
senses.definition: the second month of the calendar year, with twenty-eight days in most years
senses.definitionCN: 公历年的第二个月，多数年份有二十八天
senses.example: February is the shortest month.
senses.why: The month is named for an ancient purification festival and still sits at winter's end.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以古老的净化节命名，如今仍站在冬天的末尾。

senses.title: The last stretch of winter
senses.definition: the month seen as the cold season's final stage before spring

senses.example: February days are still short and grey.
senses.exampleCN: 二月的白天仍然又短又灰。
senses.why: Coming last in winter, the month carries the feeling of waiting for warmth.
senses.whyCN: 排在冬天的最后，这个月带着等待温暖的感觉。

senses.title: The month of leap years
senses.definition: the month that gains an extra day in a leap year

senses.example: February has twenty-nine days in a leap year.

senses.why: The shortest month is the one chosen to absorb the extra day, so it stands out on calendars.
senses.whyCN: 最短的月份被选来吸收多出的那一天，因此在日历上格外特别。

definition_en: the third month of the year, between February and April
core_image: 春风把树枝摇醒，嫩芽探出头来
scene: 三月风很大，树上的嫩芽开始冒出来。In March the wind is strong, and new buds begin to appear on the trees.
sceneCN: 这里 March 是「三月」（第 1 个义项：一年中的第三个月，在二月与四月之间）；句意：三月风很大，树上的嫩芽开始冒出来。

senses.title: The third month of the year
senses.definition: the third month of the calendar year, with thirty-one days
senses.definitionCN: 公历年的第三个月，有三十一天
senses.example: March brings longer days.
senses.why: The month is named for Mars, and it stands where winter begins to loosen.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以战神玛尔斯命名，正站在冬天开始松动的时节。

senses.title: The opening of spring
senses.definition: the month felt as the start of spring growth and warmer air
senses.definitionCN: 被感受为春天生长与暖空气开始的那个月

senses.why: New growth makes the month a symbol of waking after the cold.
senses.whyCN: 新生的枝叶让这个月成为寒冬之后苏醒的象征。

senses.title: The month in dates
senses.definition: the month name used before a date or in a yearly schedule

senses.whyCN: 有名字的月份把活动固定在日历上，所以 March 也用作日期标签。

definition_en: the fifth month of the year, between April and June
core_image: 花园里成片的花一起开放
scene: 五月花园里开满了花。In May the garden is full of flowers.

senses.why: The month is named for a spring goddess and sits at the heart of the growing season.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以春天女神命名，正处在生长季的中心。

senses.title: The height of spring flowers
senses.definition: the month seen as the peak of spring bloom

senses.example: The garden is full of flowers in May.
senses.why: Warmth and light reach a balance that lets many plants flower at once.
senses.whyCN: 温暖与光照达到平衡，让许多植物同时开花。

senses.title: The month of festivals
senses.definition: the month used for spring festivals and community celebrations

senses.whyCN: 明亮温和的月份邀请人们走到户外，因此节庆聚集在它的名字周围。

intro.en: June comes from the goddess Juno's name plus a Latin month ending.
intro.cn: June 来自女神 Juno 之名加拉丁月份词尾。

latinIntro.en: Iunius is the Latin month of Juno, queen of the gods.
latinIntro.cn: Iunius 是众神之后朱诺之月。

items.example: Juno protects marriage in old stories.
items.exampleCN: 在古老故事里 Juno 守护婚姻。
夏天大约从 June 开始。

items.meaning: a woman on her wedding day
items.example: A June bride walks under green trees.
items.exampleCN: June bride 走过绿树之下。

items.meaning: a day free from work or school

items.exampleCN: June 的日光持续得很晚。

definition_en: the seventh month of the year, between June and August
core_image: 盛夏午后，阳光把泳池照得发亮
scene: 七月我们放暑假，常去游泳。In July we are on summer holiday and often go swimming.
sceneCN: 这里 July 是「七月」（第 1 个义项：一年中的第七个月，在六月与八月之间）；句意：七月我们放暑假，常去游泳。

senses.title: The seventh month of the year
senses.definition: the seventh month of the calendar year, with thirty-one days
senses.definitionCN: 公历年的第七个月，有三十一天
senses.example: July is the hottest month here.
senses.exampleCN: 七月是这里最热的月份。
senses.why: The month is named for Julius Caesar and falls in the heat of summer.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以尤利乌斯·凯撒命名，正处在盛夏的炎热中。

senses.title: Midsummer and the summer holiday
senses.definition: the month felt as the height of summer and the heart of the long holiday
senses.definitionCN: 被感受为盛夏顶点和漫长假期的核心的那个月
senses.example: Swimming pools are busy in July.
senses.why: Heat and free time combine, so the month becomes a symbol of summer leisure.
senses.whyCN: 炎热与空闲时间结合，这个月成为夏日休闲的象征。

senses.title: The month in history and holidays
senses.definition: the month used for national holidays and historical dates
senses.definitionCN: 用于国庆节和历史日期的月份
senses.example: Many national holidays fall in July.
senses.why: Warm weather and long days make the month a common choice for national celebrations.
senses.whyCN: 温暖的天气和长日使这个月成为国庆庆祝的常见选择。

intro.en: July is the month of Julius Caesar, renamed in his honour over two thousand years ago.
intro.cn: July 是尤利乌斯·凯撒之月，两千多年前为纪念他而改名。

items.en: The month is renamed Iulius after Julius Caesar.
items.cn: 这个月以尤利乌斯·凯撒之名改称 Iulius。

items.en: The name passes into French as juillet.
items.cn: 这个名字以 juillet 进入法语。

items.en: English borrows it as Julie or July.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 Julie 或 July。

items.en: The spelling settles as July.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 July。

items.en: July remains the warm seventh month.
items.cn: 现代英语中，July 仍是炎热的第七个月。

note.en: July is the seventh month, Jul. is its short form, and August follows.
note.cn: July 是第七个月，Jul. 是缩写，August 紧随其后。

entries.definition: the short written form of July

entries.definitionCN: 常见人名朱莉，与 July 形近

entries.definition: one of the twelve divisions of the year
entries.definitionCN: 月，一年十二个分段之一
八月，七月之后的一个月

normalIntro.en: July is Caesar's month, hot and full of summer holiday.
normalIntro.cn: July 是凯撒之月，炎热又满是暑假。

normal.en: July follows June.
normal.cn: July 紧跟在 June 之后。

normal.en: Jul. is short for July.
normal.cn: Jul. 是 July 的缩写。

normal.en: July has thirty-one days.
normal.cn: July 有三十一天。

normal.en: Julius Caesar hides inside July.
normal.cn: 尤利乌斯·凯撒藏在 July 里。

normal.en: July heat sends us to the pool.
normal.cn: July heat 把我们赶到泳池。

abstract.en: Picture a bright pool under a white sun.
abstract.cn: 想象白亮太阳下的明亮泳池。

abstract.en: See a calendar month with no school days.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有上学日的日历月。

abstract.en: Feel heat rising from the pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象人行道升起的热气。

examples.en: July is the hottest month here.
examples.cn: 七月是这里最热的月份。

examples.en: Swimming pools are busy in July.
Many national holidays fall in July.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朱来」——盛夏热浪扑面而来；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 Iulius，以尤利乌斯·凯撒（Julius Caesar）命名，经古法语 juillet 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the seventh month, the peak of summer, and a season of national holidays.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词命名第七个月、盛夏顶点，以及国庆集中的时节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright pool under the full heat of summer.
core.cn: 核心意象：盛夏烈日下发亮的泳池。

branches.en: The base sense is the seventh calendar month.
branches.cn: 基本义是公历第七个月。

branches.en: The month becomes the height of summer leisure.
branches.cn: 这个月份成为夏日休闲的顶点。

branches.en: Its dates host national holidays and history.
branches.cn: 它的日期承载国庆与历史。

branches.en: Calendar position and heat make one summer image.
branches.cn: 日历位置与炎热合成同一个夏日意象。

branches.en: Free hot days gather public celebrations.
branches.cn: 炎热空闲的日子聚集公共庆祝。

intro.en: July comes from the name Julius plus a Latin month ending.
intro.cn: July 来自 Julius 之名加拉丁月份词尾。

latinIntro.en: Iulius is the Latin month name honouring Julius Caesar.
latinIntro.cn: Iulius 是纪念尤利乌斯·凯撒的拉丁月份名。

items.exampleCN: Julius 给了 July 名字。

items.example: Jul. saves room on a ticket.
items.exampleCN: Jul. 能在票面上节省空间。

items.example: Summer reaches its peak in July.
items.exampleCN: 夏天在 July 达到顶峰。

items.example: A summer holiday starts in July.
The pool is busy in July.
items.exampleCN: 泳池在 July 很热闹。
